  accrual_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.accrual. Business justification: Route exceptions trigger cost accruals for recovery costs, carrier penalties, and customer credits. Required for period-end accruals and financial statement accuracy.']
  carrier_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the carrier responsible for executing the affected route leg at the time the exception occurred. Supports carrier performance analytics and SLA breach attribution.']
  consignment_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the shipment record affected by this route exception. Enables cross-domain linkage between route exceptions and the Shipment domain for customer impact assessment.']
  driver_profile_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to fleet.driver_profile. Business justification: Route exceptions involving driver behavior (HOS violations, safety incidents, route deviations) must link to driver profiles for performance management, compliance tracking, and training needs identif']
  driver_safety_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.driver_safety_event. Business justification: Route exceptions correlate with driver safety events: speeding to recover delayed ETA, harsh braking during congestion, fatigue from extended delays. Linking supports behavioral analysis, coaching pri']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the operations staff member or team lead assigned to manage and resolve this route exception. Supports workload management and accountability tracking in Oracle TMS.']
  environmental_incident_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.environmental_incident. Business justification: Route exceptions (vehicle breakdowns, cargo spills, container damage) trigger environmental incidents (fuel leaks, hazmat releases, contamination). Linking enables environmental incident investigation']
  freight_order_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the freight order associated with this route exception. Links to the SAP TM freight order or Oracle TMS shipment execution record affected by the deviation.']
  handling_agent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to network.agent. Business justification: Agents handle exception resolution in their assigned territories (customs delays, delivery failures, etc.). Required for agent performance tracking, escalation workflows, and agent accountability in e']
  hold_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to customs.customs_hold. Business justification: Customs holds are a major source of route exceptions. Required for exception root cause analysis, SLA breach attribution to customs events, and hold-driven delay tracking. Replaces denormalized custom']
  hse_incident_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.hse_incident. Business justification: Route exceptions (delays, carrier failures, customs holds) often escalate to HSE incidents (vehicle accidents, cargo damage, driver injury). Linking enables root cause analysis, pattern detection for ']
  hub_gateway_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the hub or node in the transport network where the exception occurred or was detected. Supports hub-level exception frequency analysis and network optimization inputs to Blue Yonder.']
  plan_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent route plan against which this exception was raised. Links the exception to the planned route in SAP TM or Oracle TMS.']
  plan_leg_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific route plan leg affected by this exception. A route plan may have multiple legs; this identifies the precise leg in deviation.']
  service_corridor_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the service corridor (defined lane or trade lane) affected by this exception. Enables corridor-level exception rate analytics and supports Blue Yonder network optimization and lane performance reporting.']
  spot_quote_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to pricing.spot_quote. Business justification: Route exceptions on spot quote shipments. Spot_quote_id links exception to quoted movement, enabling spot quote exception tracking, quoted service level breach analysis, and spot quote reliability mea']
  transport_asset_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to fleet.transport_asset. Business justification: Route exceptions (delays, breakdowns, accidents) often involve specific assets; linking enables root cause analysis, maintenance correlation, asset reliability scoring, and performance impact assessme']
  transport_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.transport_document. Business justification: Route exceptions trigger document amendments, claims documentation, and exception reports. Real business process: exception resolution requires documentary evidence (damage reports, delay certificates']
  actual_etd timestamp [note: 'The actual or revised Estimated Time of Departure (ETD) for the affected route leg after the exception was raised. Compared against planned_etd to quantify departure delay.']
  affected_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the route exception occurred. Used for geographic exception analytics, regulatory reporting, and cross-border compliance tracking.']
  awb_number varchar [note: 'Air Waybill (AWB) number associated with the affected air freight shipment, if applicable. Follows IATA AWB format (airline prefix-serial number). Null for non-air transport modes.']
  bol_number varchar [note: 'Bill of Lading (BOL) or Master Bill of Lading (MBL) number for the affected ocean or road freight shipment. Null for air transport mode. Supports customs and trade compliance cross-referencing.']
  cost_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Estimated or actual incremental cost incurred as a result of the route exception, expressed in US Dollars (USD). Includes carrier surcharges, expedite fees, re-routing costs, and storage charges. Used for P&L impact analysis and OPEX reporting.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp recording when the route exception record was first persisted in the data platform. May differ from raised_timestamp if there is a lag between detection and system entry.']
  customer_notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the customer was formally notified of the route exception. Null if customer_notified_flag is false. Used for SLA compliance and customer service reporting.']
  customer_notified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the affected customer has been formally notified of the route exception and its impact on their shipment. Supports customer communication compliance and Salesforce CRM case management.']
  dangerous_goods_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the affected shipment contains dangerous goods (DG) subject to IMDG Code or ICAO Technical Instructions. Triggers enhanced exception handling protocols and regulatory notification requirements.']
  delay_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Quantified delay in minutes resulting from the route exception, calculated as the difference between revised ETA and planned ETA. Core metric for SLA breach assessment and On-Time Delivery (OTD) performance reporting.']
  destination_location_code varchar [note: 'IATA airport code, UN/LOCODE, or internal hub code identifying the planned destination point of the affected route leg. Paired with origin_location_code to define the affected Origin-Destination (O-D) lane.']
  edi_transaction_reference varchar [note: 'Identifier of the Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) transaction (e.g., EDI 214 Transportation Carrier Shipment Status Message) from the carrier that reported this exception. Null if exception source is not carrier_edi.']
  escalation_level varchar [note: 'Tier of escalation reached for this route exception, indicating the management level engaged in resolution. Null if no escalation occurred.']
  escalation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the route exception was escalated to a higher tier of management or operations due to unresolved status or critical severity. Null if the exception was not escalated.']
  exception_description varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative describing the specific circumstances of the route exception, including root cause details, operational context, and any relevant external factors (e.g., port strike, adverse weather, mechanical breakdown).']
  exception_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the route exception, used in carrier communications, Oracle TMS exception queues, and customer visibility portals. Format: REXC-{YYYY}-{sequence}.']
  exception_source varchar [note: 'System or channel through which the route exception was detected and raised. FourKites provides real-time GPS-based detection; carrier EDI provides carrier-reported events; manual indicates operations team entry. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fourkites|carrier_edi|manual|sap_tm|oracle_tms|iot_sensor|blue_yonder — promote to reference product]']
  exception_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the route exception record within the exception management workflow. Drives operational queues in Oracle TMS and FourKites visibility dashboards.']
  exception_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the exception category describing the nature of the deviation from the route plan. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: delay|missed_connection|carrier_substitution|route_diversion|customs_hold|weather_disruption|capacity_shortfall — promote to reference product]']
  fourkites_event_code varchar [note: 'External event identifier from the FourKites Real-Time Visibility Platform that triggered or corresponds to this route exception. Enables bi-directional traceability between the lakehouse exception record and the FourKites source event.']
  origin_location_code varchar [note: 'IATA airport code, UN/LOCODE, or internal hub code identifying the planned origin point of the affected route leg. Used for lane-level exception analytics and network performance reporting.']
  planned_eta timestamp [note: 'The originally planned Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) at the destination of the affected route leg. Baseline for SLA breach determination and On-Time Delivery (OTD) KPI calculation.']
  planned_etd timestamp [note: 'The originally planned Estimated Time of Departure (ETD) for the affected route leg as defined in the route plan. Baseline for delay calculation and SLA compliance measurement.']
  raised_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the route exception was first detected and raised in the system. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the deviation from plan was identified.']
  recovery_cost_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Cost incurred to execute the resolution action for the route exception, expressed in US Dollars (USD). Distinct from exception_cost_usd which captures the impact cost; this captures the remediation spend.']
  recurrence_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this exception is a recurrence of a previously recorded exception on the same route leg or lane within a defined lookback period. Supports chronic exception identification and network reliability improvement.']
  resolution_action varchar [note: 'Description of the corrective action taken to resolve the route exception (e.g., carrier substitution to alternate provider, route diversion via alternate hub, expedited re-booking, customs documentation resubmission). Sourced from Oracle TMS resolution workflow.']
  resolution_action_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the resolution action taken, enabling structured analytics on exception resolution patterns and carrier/network performance improvement initiatives.']
  resolution_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the route exception was formally resolved and closed in the exception management system. Used to calculate Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR) and SLA compliance for exception handling.']
  revised_eta timestamp [note: 'The updated Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) calculated after the exception was raised, reflecting the impact of the deviation. Sourced from FourKites predictive ETA engine or carrier-reported updates.']
  root_cause_code varchar [note: 'Standardized root cause classification code assigned during exception investigation (e.g., CARRIER_CAPACITY, PORT_CONGESTION, WEATHER, DOCUMENTATION, MECHANICAL). Supports structured root cause analysis and continuous improvement programs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: carrier_capacity|port_congestion|weather|documentation|mechanical|customs_delay|infrastructure|demand_surge — promote to reference product]']
  severity varchar [note: 'Operational severity rating of the route exception indicating business impact level. Critical exceptions trigger immediate escalation; high exceptions require same-day resolution per SLA standards.']
  sla_breach_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the route exception has caused or is projected to cause a breach of the applicable Service Level Agreement (SLA) for the affected shipment or freight order. Drives customer notification and penalty calculation workflows.']
  subtype varchar [note: 'Secondary classification providing granular detail within the exception type (e.g., under \'delay\': port_congestion, mechanical_failure, driver_shortage; under \'customs_hold\': documentation_error, inspection_hold). Supports root-cause analytics.']
  transport_mode varchar [note: 'Mode of transport for the affected route leg at the time of the exception. Determines applicable regulatory frameworks (IATA for air, IMO for ocean, DOT for road/rail) and exception handling procedures.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp recording the most recent modification to the route exception record, including status changes, resolution updates, and escalation events. Supports change tracking and SLA compliance auditing.']

  Note: 'Operational exception record raised against a route plan or route plan leg when actual execution deviates from plan. Captures exception type (delay, missed connection, carrier substitution, route diversion, customs hold, weather disruption, capacity shortfall), exception severity, affected shipment/freight order reference, affected leg, exception raised timestamp, exception source (FourKites, carrier EDI, manual), resolution action taken, resolution timestamp, and exception status (open, in-progress, resolved, escalated). SSOT for route-level exception management consumed by Oracle TMS and customer visibility.'
}

Table route.carrier_schedule {
  carrier_schedule_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the carrier schedule record in the Transport Shipping lakehouse Silver layer. Primary key for this entity.']
  carrier_agreement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to contract.carrier_agreement. Business justification: Carrier schedules (vessel/flight rotations) operate under specific carrier agreements defining rates, capacity, and service terms. Essential for schedule-to-contract reconciliation, rate validation, a']
  carrier_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the carrier (shipping line, airline, road carrier, or rail operator) that operates this schedule. Used by SAP TM for carrier selection and Oracle TMS for freight audit.']
  carrier_service_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to network.carrier_service. Business justification: Carrier schedules represent specific service offerings (express, economy, etc.). Link enables service-level performance tracking, rate application, and SLA validation against contracted service commit']
  crew_lead_employee_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Vessel/flight schedules require crew lead assignment for labor planning, certification compliance verification (IATA DG, customs broker licenses), shift scheduling, and operational accountability. Cri']
  destination_node_network_node_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the network node (port, airport, hub, depot, ICD, CFS) at which this schedule arrives. Used for ETA/ETD management and last-mile delivery zone assignment.']
  emissions_factor_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to sustainability.emissions_factor. Business justification: Carrier schedules require emission factors for service-level carbon intensity used in customer-facing green product design, quotation tools, and carrier sustainability scorecards. Standard in modern l']
  lane_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the origin-destination lane master record that this schedule serves. Links the schedule to the route domain lane definition for load optimization and carrier selection in SAP TM and Oracle TMS.']
  primary_carrier_network_node_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the network node (port, airport, hub, depot, ICD, CFS) from which this schedule departs. Supports hub-and-spoke topology and FourKites real-time visibility integration.']
  tariff_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to pricing.tariff. Business justification: Carrier schedules reference tariffs for published rates. Tariff_id links schedule to pricing, enabling schedule-based tariff rate lookup, carrier schedule costing, and published rate validation agains']
  alliance_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the ocean carrier alliance (e.g., \'2M\', \'THE Alliance\', \'Ocean Alliance\') or air cargo alliance to which this schedule belongs. Used for slot-sharing and co-loading capacity management in Blue Yonder and Oracle TMS.']
  arrival_days_of_week varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of ISO weekday numbers (1=Monday through 7=Sunday) on which this schedule arrives at the destination node. May differ from departure days for multi-day transits. Used for ETA calculation and last-mile delivery zone scheduling.']
  arrival_time timestamp [note: 'Scheduled local arrival time at the destination node in HH:mm (24-hour) format. Combined with arrival_days_of_week to determine the Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) for delivery planning and SLA entitlement matching.']
  arrival_timezone varchar [note: 'IANA timezone identifier for the destination node (e.g., \'Europe/Rotterdam\', \'Asia/Tokyo\'). Required to convert local arrival time to UTC for cross-border ETA management and FourKites real-time visibility integration.']
  capacity_teu decimal(10,2) [note: 'Maximum container capacity of this schedule expressed in Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEU). Applicable for ocean FCL/LCL services. Null for non-ocean modes. Used for load optimization in Oracle TMS and capacity planning in Blue Yonder.']
  capacity_volume_cbm decimal(12,2) [note: 'Maximum volumetric capacity in Cubic Meters (CBM) for this schedule. Used alongside DIM Weight (Dimensional Weight) calculations for air freight and LTL/LCL load optimization in Oracle TMS.']
  capacity_weight_kg decimal(12,2) [note: 'Maximum payload weight capacity in kilograms for this schedule. Applicable across all transport modes (air, ocean, road, rail). Used for load optimization in Oracle TMS and freight order management in SAP TM.']
  co2e_emission_factor decimal(10,4) [note: 'Carrier-published or calculated Carbon Dioxide Equivalent (CO2e) emission factor for this schedule in kg CO2e per tonne-km. Used for GHG (Greenhouse Gas) reporting, EU ETS compliance, CORSIA carbon offsetting calculations, and sustainability analytics.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this carrier schedule record was first ingested into the Transport Shipping lakehouse Silver layer. Audit trail field for data lineage and SOX compliance.']
  cutoff_hours_before_departure decimal(5,2) [note: 'Cargo receipt deadline expressed as the number of hours before scheduled departure by which cargo must be tendered to the carrier at the origin node. Used by SAP TM for freight order management and Oracle TMS for shipment execution planning.']
  dangerous_goods_accepted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this carrier schedule accepts dangerous goods (DG) shipments (True) or not (False). Drives compliance routing in Descartes Customs and shipment eligibility checks against IMDG Code (ocean) and ICAO Technical Instructions (air).']
  departure_days_of_week varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of ISO weekday numbers (1=Monday through 7=Sunday) on which this schedule departs (e.g., \'1,3,5\' for Mon/Wed/Fri). Used by SAP TM for departure planning and Blue Yonder for network optimization.']
  departure_time timestamp [note: 'Scheduled local departure time at the origin node in HH:mm (24-hour) format. Combined with departure_days_of_week to determine the Estimated Time of Departure (ETD) for shipment planning in SAP TM and Oracle TMS.']
  departure_timezone varchar [note: 'IANA timezone identifier for the origin node (e.g., \'America/New_York\', \'Asia/Shanghai\'). Required to convert local departure time to UTC for cross-border schedule coordination and FourKites predictive ETA calculation.']
  destination_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the destination node (e.g., \'GBR\', \'SGP\', \'BRA\'). Used for import customs declaration routing in Descartes Customs, denied party screening, and WTO trade compliance.']
  destination_port_code varchar [note: 'UN/LOCODE (5-character) for ocean/road/rail destinations or IATA 3-letter airport code for air destinations. Denormalised from the destination network node for EDI messaging, customs filing, and carrier schedule matching.']
  doc_cutoff_hours_before_departure decimal(5,2) [note: 'Deadline for submission of shipping documents (AWB, BOL, customs declarations) expressed as hours before scheduled departure. Required for Descartes Customs AMS/ISF filing compliance and carrier EDI submission.']
  edi_source_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the EDI feed or carrier data exchange channel from which this schedule record was sourced (e.g., EDIFACT IFTMCS, ANSI X12 204, carrier API). Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and Silver layer ingestion audit in the Databricks lakehouse.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'Calendar date from which this carrier schedule is valid and available for booking. Used for schedule versioning, seasonal service management, and SAP TM departure planning.']
  effective_until_date date [note: 'Calendar date after which this carrier schedule is no longer valid. Null indicates an open-ended schedule with no defined end date. Used for schedule lifecycle management and carrier contract alignment.']
  frequency_per_week varchar [note: 'Number of departures per week for this schedule on the specified lane. Used by Blue Yonder for supply chain planning, capacity allocation, and network design optimization.']
  fuel_type varchar [note: 'Primary fuel type used by the vessel, aircraft, or vehicle operating this schedule. Used for BAF (Bunker Adjustment Factor) surcharge calculation, GHG emissions reporting, and EU ETS compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: VLSFO|HFO|MGO|LNG|SAF|DIESEL|ELECTRIC|HYBRID — promote to reference product]']
  is_direct_service boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this schedule operates as a direct (non-stop) service between origin and destination nodes (True) or involves intermediate port calls / transshipment stops (False). Used for transit time accuracy and customer SLA commitments.']
  origin_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the origin node (e.g., \'CHN\', \'USA\', \'DEU\'). Used for trade compliance routing in Descartes Customs, C-TPAT/AEO screening, and cross-border regulatory reporting.']
  origin_port_code varchar [note: 'UN/LOCODE (5-character) for ocean/road/rail origins or IATA 3-letter airport code for air origins. Denormalised from the origin network node for EDI messaging, AMS filing, and carrier schedule matching without requiring a node lookup.']
  published_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the carrier published or last updated this schedule via EDI feed. Represents the principal business event time for this record. Used for schedule freshness validation and EDI reconciliation in the Databricks Silver layer.']
  ref varchar [note: 'Carrier\'s own internal reference or booking system identifier for this schedule, as received via EDI. Enables round-trip reconciliation with the carrier\'s system and supports freight audit in Oracle TMS.']
  schedule_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known carrier schedule reference number or code as published by the carrier via EDI feed. Used as the business identifier for matching against carrier EDI messages (e.g., EDIFACT IFTMCS) and for reconciliation in SAP TM and Oracle TMS.']
  schedule_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the carrier schedule record. ACTIVE: available for booking and departure planning. SUSPENDED: temporarily unavailable (e.g., port congestion, force majeure). CANCELLED: permanently discontinued. DRAFT: pending carrier confirmation. EXPIRED: past effective_until_date.']
  schedule_version varchar [note: 'Monotonically incrementing version number for this carrier schedule record, incremented each time the carrier publishes an updated schedule via EDI. Supports schedule change management and historical comparison in the Silver layer.']
  temperature_controlled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this schedule provides temperature-controlled (reefer/cold chain) capacity (True) or ambient-only service (False). Used for perishable cargo eligibility and specialized equipment allocation in SAP TM.']
  transit_time_hours decimal(6,2) [note: 'Standard published transit time in hours from origin node departure to destination node arrival for this schedule. Used as the baseline for SLA (Service Level Agreement) commitments, OTD (On-Time Delivery) KPI measurement, and Blue Yonder network optimization.']
  transport_mode varchar [note: 'Primary mode of transport for this carrier schedule. Drives carrier selection logic in SAP TM, load optimization in Oracle TMS, and customs declaration routing in Descartes Customs.']
  transshipment_port_code varchar [note: 'UN/LOCODE of the primary transshipment hub for indirect services (is_direct_service = False). Used for multi-leg ETA calculation, customs transit declaration in Descartes Customs, and FourKites milestone tracking.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this carrier schedule record was last modified in the Transport Shipping lakehouse Silver layer. Used for incremental processing, change data capture, and audit trail maintenance.']
  vgm_cutoff_hours_before_departure decimal(5,2) [note: 'Deadline for submission of Verified Gross Mass (VGM) declaration expressed as hours before scheduled departure. Mandatory for ocean shipments under SOLAS Amendment 2016. Null for non-ocean modes.']
  voyage_rotation_number varchar [note: 'Carrier-assigned voyage or rotation number for ocean services, or equivalent rotation identifier for air/rail. Used for Bill of Lading (BOL) and Master Bill of Lading (MBL) cross-referencing and port authority reporting.']

  Note: 'Published carrier schedule for a specific lane or corridor leg, capturing carrier reference, service name, origin node, destination node, transport mode, vessel/flight/train service identifier, departure day(s) of week, departure time, arrival day(s) of week, arrival time, frequency, transit time (hours), capacity (TEU/kg/CBM), cut-off time (cargo receipt deadline), effective date range, and schedule status. Sourced from carrier EDI feeds and used by SAP TM for departure planning and Oracle TMS for load optimization.'
}

Table route.lane_assignment {
  lane_assignment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the lane assignment record. Primary key.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the employee assigned to manage this lane']
  lane_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the lane being managed in this assignment']
  assignment_end_date date [note: 'Date when the employee\'s assignment to this lane ended or is scheduled to end. Null indicates an active ongoing assignment.']
  assignment_start_date date [note: 'Date when the employee\'s assignment to manage this lane became effective. Used for historical tracking and workforce planning.']
  assignment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this assignment. Active assignments are operational; suspended assignments are temporarily paused; completed assignments ended normally; terminated assignments ended prematurely.']
  certification_expiry_date date [note: 'Date when the employee\'s lane-specific certification expires. Used for compliance monitoring and renewal alerts.']
  certification_status varchar [note: 'Status of required certifications for managing this lane (e.g., customs broker license for cross-border lanes, hazmat certification for DG-permitted lanes, IATA certification for air lanes). Values: certified, pending, expired, not_required.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when this assignment record was created.']
  performance_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Performance rating for this employee\'s management of this specific lane, typically measured on metrics like on-time performance, cost optimization, compliance adherence, and customer satisfaction. Scale 0-100.']
  primary_backup_flag varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this employee is the primary responsible party for this lane or serves as a backup. Used for escalation routing and succession planning.']
  role_type varchar [note: 'The specific role or function the employee performs for this lane (e.g., lane_manager, lane_analyst, lane_coordinator, customs_specialist, hazmat_coordinator). Different roles have different responsibilities and certification requirements.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when this assignment record was last updated.']
  workload_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of the employee\'s total workload allocated to this lane. Used for capacity planning and workload balancing across multiple lane assignments. Scale 0-100.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Assignment between lane and employee. It captures the operational assignment of employees (lane managers, analysts, coordinators) to specific origin-destination lanes for management, optimization, and compliance oversight. Each record links one lane to one employee with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship, including assignment period, role type, primary/backup designation, performance metrics, and required certifications.. Existence Justification: In Transport Shipping operations, lane management requires specialized workforce assignments where multiple employees (lane managers, analysts, coordinators, customs specialists, hazmat coordinators) are simultaneously assigned to manage a single lane, and each employee manages multiple lanes across the network. This is an operational assignment process, not a reference or analytical correlation - the business actively creates, tracks, and manages these assignments with specific roles, performance metrics, certification requirements, and time periods.'
}

Table route.lane_fulfillment_allocation {
  lane_fulfillment_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the lane-fulfillment center allocation record. Primary key.']
  fulfillment_center_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the fulfillment center facility']
  lane_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the origin-destination lane in the transport network']
  allocation_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of lane capacity allocated to this fulfillment center for network load balancing and capacity planning. Used in routing optimization algorithms to distribute shipment volume across multiple centers serving the same lane.']
  allocation_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this lane-fulfillment center allocation: active (in use), suspended (temporarily disabled), expired (past effective_to_date), planned (future allocation not yet effective).']
  capacity_allocation decimal(12,2) [note: 'Maximum capacity (in CBM or weight units) allocated to this fulfillment center on this lane. Used to enforce capacity constraints during shipment routing and prevent overallocation.']
  created_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this allocation record was created in the system.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'Date from which this lane-fulfillment center allocation becomes operationally effective. Supports temporal network configuration changes and seasonal capacity adjustments.']
  effective_to_date date [note: 'Date on which this lane-fulfillment center allocation expires or is superseded. Null indicates an open-ended allocation. Supports temporal network configuration management.']
  last_modified_by varchar [note: 'User or system identifier that last modified this allocation record.']
  last_modified_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this allocation record was last updated.']
  priority_rank varchar [note: 'Priority ranking of this fulfillment center for the lane, where lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used when multiple centers can serve the same lane to determine preferred routing sequence during shipment planning.']
  volume_commitment decimal(12,2) [note: 'Committed shipment volume (in CBM or weight units) that this fulfillment center is expected to route through this lane during the effective period. Used for capacity planning and carrier contract negotiations.']
  created_by varchar [note: 'User or system identifier that created this allocation record.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the operational allocation between transport lanes and fulfillment centers in the Transport Shipping network. It captures capacity planning, network optimization, and routing decisions that determine which fulfillment centers can ship via which lanes. Each record links one lane to one fulfillment center with allocation percentages, priority rankings, volume commitments, and effective date ranges that exist only in the context of this network allocation relationship.. Existence Justification: In Transport Shipping network operations, fulfillment centers can ship via multiple lanes to reach different destinations with different service levels and carriers, while lanes can be served by multiple fulfillment centers to provide network redundancy, capacity balancing, and geographic coverage. The business actively manages these allocations through network planning processes that assign allocation percentages, priority rankings, volume commitments, and capacity limits to each center-lane pairing for routing optimization and capacity planning.'
}

Table route.lane_surcharge_application {
  lane_surcharge_application_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this specific surcharge application to a lane. Primary key.']
  lane_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key to route.lane identifying which lane this surcharge applies to']
  pricing_surcharge_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key to pricing.surcharge identifying which surcharge is being applied']
  application_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this surcharge application to the lane. Allows temporary suspension of surcharges on specific lanes without removing the configuration.']
  calculation_method varchar [note: 'The calculation method used for this specific lane-surcharge combination, which may differ from the default surcharge calculation method to accommodate lane-specific pricing rules.']
  created_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this surcharge application record was created in the system.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'Date on which this surcharge application expires for the specific lane. Null indicates open-ended application.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'Date from which this surcharge application becomes active for the specific lane. Allows lane-specific surcharge timing that may differ from the global surcharge definition dates.']
  last_modified_by varchar [note: 'User or system identifier that last modified this surcharge application record.']
  last_modified_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this surcharge application record.']
  maximum_charge_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Lane-specific maximum surcharge amount that caps the calculation result for this particular lane.']
  minimum_charge_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Lane-specific minimum surcharge amount that overrides the global surcharge minimum for this particular lane.']
  override_reason varchar [note: 'Business justification for why this lane has different surcharge parameters than the global surcharge definition (e.g., competitive pressure, regulatory requirement, contract exception).']
  surcharge_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'The specific surcharge amount applicable to this lane, which may override or supplement the base surcharge definition amount based on lane-specific factors.']
  created_by varchar [note: 'User or system identifier that created this surcharge application record.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the application of a specific surcharge to a specific lane. It captures the effective pricing rules, calculation parameters, and temporal validity for each surcharge-lane combination. Each record links one surcharge definition to one lane with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, enabling dynamic surcharge management across the lane network.. Existence Justification: In logistics operations, surcharges are applied to multiple lanes (e.g., a fuel surcharge applies across all Asia-Pacific lanes, a peak season surcharge applies to high-volume lanes during Q4), and each lane has multiple surcharges applied simultaneously (fuel, security, terminal handling, war risk). The business actively manages these applications with lane-specific effective dates, amounts, and calculation parameters that differ from the global surcharge definitions.'
}

  compliance_status varchar [note: 'Current compliance status of this certification requirement for the schedule. COMPLIANT: certification is valid and verified; NON_COMPLIANT: certification missing, expired, or insufficient; PENDING_VERIFICATION: awaiting verification; EXEMPTION_GRANTED: regulatory exemption applies; EXPIRED: certification has expired.']

Existence Justification: In logistics operations, carrier schedules (flights, vessel voyages, rail services) that transport dangerous goods must comply with multiple regulatory certifications depending on the DG classes being carried. Table route.lane_facility_service {

  Note: 'This association product represents the operational service configuration between a transport lane and a warehouse facility. Each record links one facility to one lane with attributes that exist only in the context of this lane-facility service relationship, supporting network optimization, capacity planning, and route assignment decisions.. Existence Justification: In Transport Shipping\'s logistics network, facilities and lanes have a genuine many-to-many operational relationship. A single facility (warehouse/DC) serves as origin, destination, or intermediate node for multiple lanes (e.g., LAX facility serves LAX-JFK, LAX-ORD, LAX-SEA lanes). Conversely, a single lane connects multiple facilities in hub-and-spoke or multi-stop routing scenarios (e.g., the Asia-Europe lane may route through Singapore hub, Dubai hub, and Amsterdam hub facilities). The business actively manages lane-facility service configurations with priority rankings, capacity allocations, and facility-specific SLA commitments for network optimization.'

Each record links one fulfillment center to one safety program with attributes that exist only in the context of this enrollment relationship.. Existence Justification: In Transport Shipping logistics operations, fulfillment centers participate in multiple safety programs simultaneously (OSHA VPP, ISO 45001, hazmat handling certifications, driver safety programs), and each safety program covers multiple facilities across the network. Safety managers actively manage these enrollments as operational entities, tracking compliance status, conducting facility-specific audits, assigning local coordinators, and monitoring certification levels for each facility-program combination. This is not a reference relationship but an actively managed business process with substantial relationship-specific data.'
}

Table fulfillment.service {
  service_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this center-carrier service agreement. Primary key.']
  carrier_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the carrier partner providing service']
  fulfillment_center_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the fulfillment center facility being served']
  capacity_allocation decimal(12,2) [note: 'Daily shipment capacity (in cubic meters or weight units) allocated to this carrier at this fulfillment center. Used for capacity planning and load balancing across multiple carrier partners.']
  days varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of days of the week this carrier provides pickup service at this fulfillment center (e.g., Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri). Service days vary by facility location and carrier route coverage.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this center-carrier service agreement became effective. Used to track historical service configurations and support time-based queries.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date when this center-carrier service agreement expires or was terminated. Null indicates an active ongoing agreement. Used for contract lifecycle management.']
  pickup_cutoff_time timestamp [note: 'Daily cutoff time (HH:MM 24-hour format) by which shipments must be ready for carrier pickup at this specific fulfillment center. Varies by carrier and facility based on route schedules.']
  priority_rank varchar [note: 'Priority ranking of this carrier for shipments from this fulfillment center (1=highest priority). Used in carrier selection logic when multiple carriers serve the same center.']
  service_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this center-carrier service relationship. Values: active (operational), suspended (temporarily paused), terminated (ended), pending (not yet active).']

  Note: 'This association product represents the operational service agreement between a fulfillment center and a carrier partner. It captures center-specific pickup schedules, service day configurations, and capacity allocations that exist only in the context of this facility-carrier relationship. Each record links one fulfillment center to one carrier with operational parameters that govern how that carrier serves that specific facility.. Existence Justification: In Transport Shipping logistics operations, fulfillment centers are served by multiple carrier partners simultaneously for redundancy, capacity, and service coverage, and each carrier serves multiple fulfillment centers across the network. The business actively manages center-specific service agreements that define pickup schedules, cutoff times, service days, and capacity allocations that vary by facility-carrier combination. These operational parameters cannot be stored on either the center or carrier entity alone because they exist only in the context of the specific facility-carrier relationship.'
}

It captures the completion status, certification validity, and recertification scheduling for each merchant-training combination. Each record links one merchant to one safety training course with attributes that exist only in the context of this compliance relationship.. Existence Justification: In Transport Shipping logistics operations, merchants who ship dangerous goods (lithium batteries, hazmat, etc.) must maintain multiple safety training certifications mandated by different regulatory bodies (IATA DGR, DOT, ADR). Each training course applies to multiple merchants based on their product mix and shipping lanes. The compliance team actively manages this many-to-many relationship by tracking completion dates, certificate numbers, recertification schedules, and cost allocation for each merchant-training combination, generating training matrix reports for regulatory audits.'
}

  penalty_triggered_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this volume shortfall has triggered a contractual penalty clause. True if penalty conditions are met, False otherwise.']
  period_type varchar [note: 'The type of measurement period used for volume tracking. Aligns with contract terms and billing cycles.']

  surplus_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the actual volume shipped exceeded the committed volume for this period. True if actual > committed, False otherwise.']

  volume_unit varchar [note: 'The unit of measure used for both actual and committed volumes. Common units include TEU (Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit) for containers, kg for weight-based commitments, CBM (Cubic Meter) for dimensional volume, or shipment count for parcel-based agreements.']
  volume_variance decimal(18,3) [note: 'The difference between actual volume shipped and committed volume (actual minus committed). Positive values indicate surplus, negative values indicate shortfall.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of actual volumes shipped against contracted volume commitments for each measurement period. Captures period start and end dates, actual volume shipped (TEU, kg, CBM, shipment count), committed volume, variance, attainment percentage, and shortfall or surplus flag. Used to trigger penalty or incentive clause calculations and contract compliance reporting.'

  penalty_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Fixed penalty amount or base penalty value applied when the clause is triggered (in contract currency). Null if calculation is percentage-based or tiered.']
  penalty_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage rate applied to calculate the penalty or incentive (e.g., 2.5 for 2.5% of invoice value). Null if calculation is fixed-fee based.']

  trigger_condition varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the condition or event that activates this penalty or incentive clause (e.g., OTD below 95%, volume below 1000 TEU per month, payment received after 60 days).']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version number of this penalty or incentive clause, incremented with each amendment or revision to the clause terms.']

  Note: 'Defines financial clauses embedded within a contract, encompassing both penalty clauses (SLA breach penalties, volume shortfall penalties, late payment penalties, service failure deductions) and incentive/rebate clauses (volume rebates, performance bonuses for exceeding OTD/OTIF targets, loyalty discounts, early payment incentives). Captures clause type (penalty or incentive), trigger condition/threshold, calculation method (fixed fee, percentage of invoice, credit note, tiered rebate, flat bonus), maximum liability cap or maximum payout, cure period, escalation path, payment frequency, and accrual method. Linked to the parent agreement and specific SLA or volume commitment.'
}

  waived_by varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the person who authorized the waiver of this penalty event.']
  waiver_date date [note: 'Date on which the penalty was waived.']
  waiver_reason varchar [note: 'Business justification for waiving the penalty or not applying the incentive, if status is waived.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of an actual penalty or incentive event triggered under a contract clause. Captures the triggering event (SLA breach, volume shortfall, service failure), event date, calculated penalty or incentive amount, currency, status (pending, approved, disputed, settled), reference to the billing domain for credit/debit note issuance, and resolution notes.'

  Note: 'This association product represents the service assignment contract between a commercial agreement and a supplier. It captures the specific terms, rates, commitments, and SLAs that apply when a particular supplier provides services under a specific agreement. Each record links one agreement to one supplier with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, enabling multi-vendor service delivery models where a single customer agreement is fulfilled by multiple carriers, brokers, warehouse providers, or other logistics service providers.. Existence Justification: In logistics operations, a single customer service agreement frequently requires multiple suppliers to fulfill different service components: a primary ocean carrier, a backup carrier for capacity overflow, a customs broker for clearance, a warehouse provider for storage, and last-mile delivery partners. Conversely, a single supplier (e.g., a major carrier like Maersk or DHL) serves hundreds of different customer agreements with varying rates, SLAs, and volume commitments specific to each agreement-supplier pairing. This is an operational M:N relationship that contract managers actively maintain.'
}

The business actively manages these documentation requirements with obligation-specific retention periods, verification schedules, and compliance status tracking.'

  benefit_expiry_date date [note: 'Date when the compliance program benefits expire for this agreement. May differ from the programs general expiry_date based on agreement-specific terms or renewal cycles.']
  compliance_program varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the compliance program applicable to this agreement, such as Customs-Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (C-TPAT) or Authorized Economic Operator (AEO). Determines security and audit requirements. [Moved from agreement: The compliance_program attribute in the agreement table is a STRING field that appears to store a single program name or identifier. This is insufficient for the true M:N business reality where agreements can be qualified by multiple compliance programs simultaneously (e.g., AEO for EU lanes, C-TPAT for US lanes). This attribute should be removed from agreement and replaced by the M:N association, which allows multiple programs per agreement with program-specific qualification details.]']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this qualification record was created in the system']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this qualification record was last modified']
  program_benefit_tier varchar [note: 'Tier or level of customs benefits that this specific compliance program confers to this specific agreement (e.g., Standard, Enhanced, Premium). Benefit tier may vary by agreement based on volume, lanes, or negotiated terms.']
  program_reference_date date [note: 'Date when this compliance program was first referenced or associated with this agreement during contract negotiation or execution']
  qualification_verification_status varchar [note: 'Current verification status of this compliance program qualification for this agreement. Tracks whether the program benefits are actively applicable to shipments under this agreement.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the qualification relationship between compliance programs and commercial agreements. It captures which trusted trader programs (C-TPAT, AEO, etc.) qualify specific service agreements for customs benefits, including program-specific benefit tiers, qualification dates, and verification status. Each record links one compliance_program to one agreement with attributes that exist only in the context of this qualification relationship.. Existence Justification: In Transport Shipping logistics operations, a single compliance program (such as AEO or C-TPAT) can qualify multiple commercial service agreements for customs benefits, and a single agreement can legitimately reference multiple compliance programs simultaneously to cover different trade lanes (e.g., AEO for EU shipments, C-TPAT for US shipments under the same master agreement). The business actively manages these qualifications with program-specific benefit tiers, verification statuses, and effective dates that vary by agreement.'
}

Covers loss, damage, shortage, delay, contamination, and dangerous goods claims across all transport modes (air, ocean, road, rail). Includes incident event details (date, location, circumstances, transport mode) and claim type classification. Aligned to IMO, IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention, CMR Convention, and Hague-Visby liability frameworks. Serves as the SSOT for all claim identity, status, valuation, and lifecycle data.'

  is_dangerous_goods boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the cargo involved in the incident is classified as dangerous goods under IMDG Code (ocean), ICAO Technical Instructions (air), or ADR/RID (road/rail). Triggers mandatory regulatory notification and specialist DG survey procedures.']
  liability_convention varchar [note: 'International liability convention applicable to this cargo incident based on transport mode and route. Determines the carrier liability limit (e.g., SDR per kg under Montreal Convention, SDR per package under Hague-Visby). Drives settlement calculation methodology.']
  liability_limit_sdr decimal(18,2) [note: 'Calculated maximum carrier liability for this incident expressed in IMF Special Drawing Rights (SDR), derived from the applicable convention limit and cargo weight or package count. Used as the ceiling for settlement calculations and insurer reserve setting.']
  number_of_pieces varchar [note: 'Total number of individual pieces, packages, or units in the consignment involved in the incident. Used to quantify shortage claims and assess the scope of damage surveys.']
  origin_country varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the shipment origin at the time of the incident. Used for jurisdictional liability determination and cross-border regulatory reporting.']
  reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to the cargo incident event at the time of registration. Used in insurer correspondence, survey reports, and claimant communications. Format: CE-{YYYY}-{8-digit sequence}.']
  reported_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which the cargo incident was formally reported to Transport Shipping by the claimant, consignee, or shipper. Used to calculate notification compliance against convention time-bar requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Operational system of record from which the claim event was originated or first captured. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation between source systems. Salesforce CRM is the primary source for customer-reported incidents; FourKites for visibility-triggered exceptions.']
  survey_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a physical cargo survey by an independent surveyor or loss adjuster is required for this incident. Determined by incident type, declared value threshold, and insurer requirements. Triggers survey dispatch workflow.']
  time_bar_date date [note: 'Calculated deadline by which a formal cargo claim must be filed under the applicable liability convention before the right to claim is extinguished. Derived from incident date and convention-specific time limits (e.g., 2 years under Montreal Convention, 1 year under Hague-Visby). Critical for claims management SLA monitoring.']
  transport_mode varchar [note: 'Mode of transport in operation at the time of the cargo incident. Determines the applicable liability convention (IATA Warsaw-Montreal for air, Hague-Visby/Hamburg Rules for ocean, CMR for road, CIM/COTIF for rail). Drives insurer notification and survey requirements.']
  un_number varchar [note: 'United Nations dangerous goods identification number for the hazardous substance involved in the incident. Mandatory for IMDG and ICAO DG incident reporting. Null if is_dangerous_goods is False. Format: UN followed by 4-digit number (e.g., UN1203).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when the claim event record was last modified. Supports change tracking and audit compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  volume_cbm decimal(12,3) [note: 'Total volume of the cargo consignment involved in the incident, expressed in cubic metres (CBM). Used for volumetric assessment of damage extent and DIM weight calculations for air freight liability.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing the initiating loss or damage event that triggers a cargo claim. Records the incident date, location, transport mode, event type (loss, damage, shortage, delay, contamination, dangerous goods incident), and initial circumstances. Provides the factual basis for liability determination and insurer correspondence. One claim event may generate one or more cargo claims.'
}

  loss_event_date date [note: 'Date on which the cargo loss, damage, delay, or other qualifying event occurred that gave rise to the original claim and subsequent subrogation right.']
  loss_event_location varchar [note: 'Geographic location (port, terminal, warehouse, road segment, airport) where the cargo loss or damage event occurred. Determines jurisdiction and applicable liability convention.']
  opened_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the subrogation case was formally opened following settlement of the originating cargo claim. Marks the start of the recovery pursuit period.']
  recovery_amount_received decimal(18,2) [note: 'Actual monetary amount recovered from the respondent party to date. Populated incrementally as payments are received and updated upon final case closure.']
  recovery_amount_sought decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total monetary amount being demanded from the respondent party in the subrogation recovery action. May differ from the settlement amount due to contributory negligence, liability caps, or partial recovery strategy.']
  recovery_currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which recovery amounts are denominated and tracked for this subrogation case.']
  recovery_rate_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of the recovery amount sought that was actually recovered from the respondent party. Calculated as (recovery_amount_received / recovery_amount_sought) * 100. Key KPI for subrogation P&L performance tracking.']
  reserve_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Financial reserve amount set aside in the general ledger for the expected net recovery from this subrogation case. Used for reserve accounting and financial reporting under IFRS.']
  respondent_insurer_name varchar [note: 'Name of the respondent party\'s liability insurer, if known. Relevant when recovery is pursued against the respondent\'s insurance policy rather than directly against the respondent.']
  respondent_insurer_policy_number varchar [note: 'Policy number of the respondent party\'s liability insurance policy against which the subrogation recovery is being pursued.']
  respondent_party_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the liable third-party respondent against whom recovery is sought. Determines applicable liability framework and legal jurisdiction. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sub_carrier|port_operator|customs_authority|freight_handler|warehouse_operator|nvocc|terminal_operator — promote to reference product]']
  respondent_response_date date [note: 'Date on which the respondent party formally responded to the subrogation demand letter, either accepting, partially accepting, or disputing liability.']
  settlement_date date [note: 'Date on which a negotiated settlement agreement was reached with the respondent party, resolving the subrogation recovery action without full legal proceedings.']
  statute_of_limitations_date date [note: 'Date by which legal action must be commenced against the respondent party under the applicable liability convention or domestic law. Critical for case management and legal filing deadlines.']
  transport_mode varchar [note: 'Mode of transport applicable to the underlying cargo loss event, determining which international liability convention governs the subrogation claim (e.g., Warsaw-Montreal for air, CMR for road, Hague-Visby for ocean).']

  Note: 'Master record managing the subrogation process where the insurer or carrier pursues recovery from a liable third party (sub-carrier, port operator, customs authority, freight handler) after settling a cargo claim. Captures subrogation target party, recovery amount sought, legal proceedings status, and case closure outcome. Includes individual recovery action tracking: demand letters, legal filings, arbitration proceedings, settlement negotiations, amounts demanded vs. recovered, and action outcomes. Aligned to international subrogation rights under CMR, Warsaw-Montreal, Hague-Visby, and marine insurance law. Supports recovery P&L tracking and third-party liability management.'
}
